You can use modal verbs to talk about uncertain events in the past.

You use these structures to talk about the past. Each one has slightly different meaning, but they all imply uncertainty and speculation.

  • must have + past participle

  • might / might not have + past participle

  • could / couldn't have + past participle

  • may / may not have + past participle

  • can't have + past participle


You : Where was Dave last night?
Jason:
He must have forgotten about our plans.
He might have worked late.
He could have taken the wrong bus.
He may have felt ill.
He can't have stayed at home.
The staff may be busy and might have forgotten about the playlist.
They may have felt a younger sound would make that place seem more energetic.
That kind of music might have worked in another locale.
They could have thought that's the style nowadays.
People can't have enjoyed themselves in there, could they?
So introduces a clause that expresses an effect (result) of the cause expressed in the main clause.

For example:

He saw an old lady struggling with her bags, so her helped her.
You use a comma to separate the so clause from the main clause.
I heard it had amazing desserts, so I thought we should try it.
I have finished my diet last week, so now I can have some cheese cake.

images.text:
Amy: Is this the place, V?
Vanessa: I heard it had amazing desserts, so I thought we should try it.
Peter: It's cool looking. This place has a certain quality, but listen to the music they are playing.

Amy: Yeah. It doesn't really suit the ambiance of this place, does it?
Vanessa: They have stylish decor, but it's like they left a teenage girl in charge of the music.The staff may be busy and might have forgotten about the playlist.
Vanessa: I finished my diet last week, so now I can have some cheese cake.
Peter: Huh? You are on a diet.

Vanessa: YES. I mean NO. I was, but now ... I'm NOT.
Amy: I ate only a salad for dinner, so I'm going to have the chocolate cake.
Vanessa & Peter: WHAT?
Peter: It's too loud, so I can't hear what you are saying.

Vanessa: Excuse me, miss? Is there anyway you could turn down the music a little?
Server: I'm sorry. It's company policy so we are not allowed to change the music. Sorry. Are you ready to order?
Vanessa: Give us one more minute, please. Guys, it's too loud. Do you want to stay? Excuse me, Miss. It's just too loud in here, so we are going to have to leave.

Server: Ok. Sorry about that.
Peter: That was crazy in there. That kind of music might have worked in another locale, but it didn't work there.
Amy: They may have felt a younger sound would make that place seem more energetic and appeal to a younger crowd or they could have thought that's the style nowadays.
Peter: They must have forgotten who their clientele was. Everyone in their was in their 30's.
Vanessa: People can't have enjoyed themselves in there, could they? The server didn't help, for she knew she could do nothing.
Peter: I don't know. Maybe we are getting old?
